classifications.explicit_policy: Rationale explicitly documented in source/tests/maintainer decisions.
classifications.platform_constraint: Native API, runtime, hardware or installation prerequisite; not universal OS impossibility unless established.
classifications.guarded_unimplemented: Deliberately safe refusal around an unfinished capability; NOT a product decision to omit it.
classifications.observed_not_decided: Behavior is evidenced but product intent or desired cross-OS equivalence is not established.
classifications.shared_policy: Current implementations share the policy; an older OS-specific claim was refuted.

differences.title: Programmable source process and state lifetime

behavior.windows: AHK factory/callback runs in an isolated native Job process; execution can recreate state. The mechanism is explicit; unequal closure-state lifetime is a derived consequence without a separately established product decision.
behavior.macos: Lua factory callbacks run in the retained Lua owner outside the input hook.
behavior.linux: Lua callbacks use the shared owner and deferred loop scheduling.

differences.title: Who owns the completing physical key

behavior.windows: Usually observes already delivered input and compensates; Enter/Tab have dedicated interception.
behavior.macos: Consumes the completing event and owns native terminator replay.
behavior.linux: Observed evdev/uinput flow compensates already forwarded input.

behavior.windows: Current HSE_ComplexDelayMultiplier reads the shared multiplier/carry registry.
behavior.macos: Complex modifier movement widens eligible expansion windows, excluding autocorrection.
behavior.linux: ExpansionDelay.allows uses the same shared multiplier/carry rule.

behavior.windows: Tests explicitly pin @dt/@td/@date and continuation behavior.
behavior.macos: Shared dynamic rules use bare dt/td/date and word boundaries.
behavior.linux: Same bare shared rules; no cross-OS decision to preserve the difference is established.

behavior.windows: No host/runtime supplied for the physical editor.
behavior.macos: Native capture/bridge exists but actual physical_delivery_available returns false.
behavior.linux: Actual delivery getter likewise returns false and gates bridge/menu. The intentional safety refusal is not a settled decision to omit the feature.

differences.title: Hold picker and native modifier vocabulary

behavior.windows: PC Ctrl/Shift/Alt/AltGr/Win combinations; native key identity is process-wide.
behavior.macos: Option/Command/Fn native hold catalogue, with different IDs and meaningful combinations.
behavior.linux: PC modifier combinations with evdev native key identities; device observation does not imply per-device assignments.

behavior.windows: Selected typing keys classify by release order and timeout.
behavior.macos: Karabiner prioritizes native typing at next key-down before hold threshold.
behavior.linux: Release-order classification; minimum-tap implementation differs in scope.

behavior.windows: Scope transactions, ordinary setters and layout selection have different terminal receipt owners. Pending receipt is not proof of applied state.
behavior.macos: Some layer/editor saves intentionally close after accepted regeneration; later native readiness is separate.
behavior.linux: Some ordinary setting changes retain saved intent after live reload/apply refusal; scope rollback is a separate owner.

differences.title: Native gesture signal and axis vocabulary

behavior.windows: Ten Precision Touchpad hotkey slots; discrete finished gestures.
behavior.macos: Native contacts permit continuous/scaled axes as well as discrete actions.
behavior.linux: Finished discrete evdev gestures; three declared horizontal axis slots are unsupported, a confirmed capability defect rather than supported axes.

behavior.windows: Configures its own Precision Touchpad shortcut mappings with backup/restore.
behavior.macos: Reads native gesture settings and asks users to remove overlaps; must not silently edit them. Current conflict defects are separately tracked.
behavior.linux: No recommended bindings while observing without a grab, avoiding duplicate desktop actions; two-finger coexistence must not be advertised as exclusive capture.

differences.title: Native pass-through, capture timing and pause exceptions

behavior.windows: Original physical-key replay on pause can be custody-preserving, not an unwanted synthetic feature action.
behavior.macos: Capture timestamps, drag/scroll guards and runtime teardown differ from finished-hotkey systems.
behavior.linux: Script-management gestures may operate while paused; other actions are gated. Failed reader recovery can require user re-enable.

differences.title: Local AI backends and streaming conditions

behavior.windows: Ollama/local API/cloud; tooltip token display is explicitly unvalidated/disabled.
behavior.macos: Adds supported Apple-Silicon MLX; remote APIs are nonstreaming while supported local paths stream.
behavior.linux: Ollama/local servers/cloud; remote requests are nonstreaming, local supported streams can update offers.

behavior.windows: Inline auto-type inserts a completed final continuation; it is not token-by-token document typing.
behavior.macos: Offers predictions for acceptance; no equivalent automatic continuation mode.
behavior.linux: Offers predictions for acceptance; absence of this mode is not proof the OS could never implement it.

differences.title: Accepted work across pause or UI retirement

behavior.windows: Some already accepted operations retain ownership; queued accepted-agent cancellation policy is unresolved, so WL-001 was removed from confirmed findings.
behavior.macos: Accepted text can survive cleanup refusal and accepted update work can continue after page close/pause. These explicit policies do not prove every agent continuation is intended.
behavior.linux: Operations have individual cancellation/admission owners; no universal cancellation rule is inferred from different callback shapes.

behavior.windows: Per-device append-only SQL ledgers, rebuildable resident/durable reader projections.
behavior.macos: Append-only journal/ledger, cache and foreign-device import/replay.
behavior.linux: Direct local metrics.sqlite, currently no equivalent ledger synchronization. This architectural limitation is not a settled product decision to omit synchronization.

differences.title: Content filtering versus metadata and machine counters

behavior.windows: Private triggers can retain numeric savings while redacting content; collection pause and driver pause differ.
behavior.macos: Private-window guarantee explicitly targets key content, not all title metadata. User collection-pause defects are separate from that policy.
behavior.linux: Unknown accessibility context fails closed for text; machine aggregates may continue independently of the raw-event recording switch.

differences.title: Pointer, CPU, Wi-Fi and awake counter semantics

behavior.windows: Screen-position samples, native system utilization and explicit passive keep-awake rollup; heuristic telemetry must remain labelled heuristic.
behavior.macos: Sampled screen displacement and CPU user share; keep-awake aggregation defects are separate.
behavior.linux: Raw pointer device units, no evdev tap-to-click; Wi-Fi can fall back to interface identity; awake_ms measures unlocked sampled uptime. Cross-OS equivalence/product intent is not established.

behavior.windows: Typed text/per-key SQL fields encrypted; aggregates clear by design. Raw plaintext journal exposure is a separate finding, not justified by the aggregate exception.
behavior.macos: Selective payload encryption and local journal/ledger ownership; no assumption of full-document or whole-disk encryption.
behavior.linux: Direct-store cipher has supported-runtime requirements; aggregates remain clear. Field scope is not a promise of universal cross-device decryption.

behavior.windows: Portable executable/source/install authorities differ; source is not self-replacement authority.
behavior.macos: Application/Sparkle and designated-requirement replacement owners; selected historical releases use a separate verified path.
behavior.linux: Standalone owner may self-replace; package manager or immutable distribution owns its updates.

behavior.windows: Shipped shared detached P-256 signature enforcement remains off pending key provisioning; digest/origin policy is distinct from Authenticode.
behavior.macos: Sparkle uses its separate signed enclosure/appcast trust path.
behavior.linux: Shares the shipped P-256 off policy; native verification/directory publication require the supported LuaJIT runtime. Verification code presence is not proof signatures are required by default.

behavior.windows: Can list Atom releases but refuses install without authenticated asset details.
behavior.macos: Newest eligible feed offer can hand off to signed Sparkle metadata; not arbitrary historical Atom installation.
behavior.linux: Lists feed releases but refuses unauthenticated asset replacement.

differences.title: Filtered overlay backups and native custody

behavior.windows: TOML/JSON config backup with handle-held restoration, personal data retained by uninstall. No proven delete-new-files snapshot contract.
behavior.macos: Filtered config root, native hs.settings excluded; POSIX staging/readback has different custody limits. Restore overlay must not be described as a full directory rollback.
behavior.linux: Includes settings store in addition to config root; filtered overlay, pre-image and named partial/refusal outcomes. Programmable source/data archives are not a complete backup promise.

behavior.windows: Rich local error/log context is preserved; sharing redacts, with explicit local-rich rationale.
behavior.macos: Local report builds/writes share schema; whole-document-at-rest redaction policy not established by the inspected path.
behavior.linux: Captured redactor processes the complete encoded report before opening the output file. No actual secret disclosure is inferred solely from this difference.

differences.title: Setup, optional imports and native prerequisites

behavior.windows: WebView2/Windows input owners and optional import outcomes have explicit acknowledgement; no native execution in this audit.
behavior.macos: Accessibility/Automation/native registration approval and signing mode qualify startup. Failed Finish partial-publication is not an intentional exception.
behavior.linux: Graphical/setup tools, input groups/session and LuaJIT native capabilities qualify support. Optional tap/layer import may notify failure after main answers commit deliberately.
